question: What Is the Working Principle of a Synchronous Motor?
body_html:
A synchronous motor works by locking its rotor to the rotating magnetic field made by the three phase stator winding, so it runs at exactly synchronous speed whatever the load.

Speed is set only by frequency and poles: Ns = 120 × f ÷ P. A 4 pole motor on 50 Hz runs at 120 × 50 ÷ 4 = 1500 rpm.

It is not self starting, so a damper winding, pony motor or VFD brings it near synchronous speed before DC excitation locks it in step.
